newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen mixed, eye trade data, tech stocks.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen mixed, eye trade data, tech stocks.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to slighly positive on Wednesday, although July international trade figures due before the opening bell could influence the opening.

Tech stocks will be closely watched after a rally ignited by Intel Corp helped U.S. stocks rebound from an almost 40 point low to close less than half a point down at the close of yesterday's session.

"We'll probably have a mixed to higher opening. If the trade numbers come in friendly, the market could move higher, but unless its very positive it should have little influence," said Westfalia Investments director of research Peter Cardillo.
At 0830 EDT/1230 GMT the Commerce Department issues its July trade report, with a deficit of $8.8 billion expected, compared to the prior month's deficit of $8.1 billion.

Larry Wachtel, market analyst for Prudential Securities said, "This should be a mixed bag session ... Watch the tech stocks. They were instrumental in allowing the market to snap back. Bonds will probably be passive as we head into the Fed meeting next Tuesday".
Analysts said program trading ahead of Friday's "triple-witching" expiration of options could also mean more active trading.
The benchmark 30 year bond was unchanged with a yield of 7.03 percent and Standard & Poor's December futures were off 1.05 to 688.90.
Tokyo stocks closed lower, with the Nikkei 225 down 153.84 points to 21,156.75 after profit-taking cut into the strong gains over the past two trading days.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 11.3 to 3961. U.S. stocks were mostly lower in London, with tech and tobacco stocks hurt by profit-taking in the aftermath of yesterday's gains.
The dollar was in narrow ranges in quiet Europe trading.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reported that FoxMeyer Health Corp's bankruptcy filing has created disputes between several securities firms and some of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies,

According to the New York Times' Marketplace column,Brooklyn Union Gas Co is implementing a new strategy that goes beyond its proposed name change to include new acquisition investments overseas and in non-core businesses,
